The quarter-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040842/assets/5234672d8176a0a04bbc3feecfe13092ff116a25682ae055286f1fe858b8a754.png)

The half-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -1,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2.
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$ Assume $\theta $ is between $0$ and $2\pi .$

$\theta \in [${{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$]$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +h,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +k,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, the ellipse is centered at the point $(-1,2),$ $a=5,$ and $b=3.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -1,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a half-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the central angle formed by a point $(x,y)$ on the ellipse and the horizontal line through its center.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040842/assets/1b2d7617af37197dfd2702b4497263e563458b0bf11c622308220def93b688a9.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2}],$ we get the half-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the half-ellipse are 

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -1,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2,\,\theta \in [\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2}].
$$
